docs.title: _fallback_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:

Description: Formulates beta header lists and extra_body payload mappings to activate server-side fallback routines on eligible models based on the ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS environment variable.

Implementation: 

def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
    """Return (betas, extra_body) for server-side refusal fallbacks, or empty when disabled."""
    setting = (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS") or "default").strip()
    if _fallbacks_disabled or setting.lower() == "off":
        return [], {}
    if setting.lower() == "default":
        if not _matches(model, _FALLBACK_PREFIXES):
            return [], {}
        return [_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA], {"fallbacks": "default"}
    targets = [m.strip() for m in setting.split(",") if m.strip()]
    return [_FALLBACK_LIST_BETA], {"fallbacks": [{"model": m} for m in targets]}
The helper evaluates ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS (defaulting to "default"). If fallbacks have been runtime-disabled via _fallbacks_disabled or explicitly set to "off", it returns empty containers. When configured to "default", it verifies whether the model matches _FALLBACK_PREFIXES (claude-opus-5, claude-fable-5), returning the beta header server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 and body {"fallbacks": "default"}. If given a custom comma-separated list of models, it returns header server-side-fallback-2026-06-01 and a structured list of target model objects.

Parameters: * model (str): Target model name.

Returns: * tuple[list[str], dict]: A 2-tuple containing a list of beta header flags and an extra_body parameter dictionary.

Example: 

# Extracted from _build_request implementation
betas, extra_body = _fallback_config(model)
if extra_body:
    params["extra_body"] = extra_body
return params, betas

docs.title: _build_request()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:

Description: Builds the complete parameter dictionary and beta headers for the Anthropic Messages API, handling adaptive thinking, fixed budget tokens, prompt caching, and fallback configurations.

Implementation: 

def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    params = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    }
    if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
        if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
            thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
            if is_debug():
                # Readable reasoning summaries go to the log file (never to stdout).
                thinking["display"] = "summarized"
            params["thinking"] = thinking
        if effort:
            params["output_config"] = {"effort": effort}
    elif effort:
        budget = min(_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL[effort], max_tokens - 1_024)
        if budget >= 1_024:
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": budget}

    if (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE") or "off").strip().lower() == "on":
        params["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}

    betas, extra_body = _fallback_config(model)
    if extra_body:
        params["extra_body"] = extra_body
    return params, betas
Initializes the base dictionary with model, max_tokens, and the single user prompt message. If the model supports adaptive thinking, it injects thinking: {"type": "adaptive"} (adding "display": "summarized" when debug logging is enabled) and maps effort to output_config: {"effort": effort}. For legacy models with thinking enabled, it calculates an integer budget_tokens clamped to max_tokens - 1024. If ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE is enabled, it sets cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}. Finally, it attaches fallback headers and payload bodies from _fallback_config().

Parameters: * prompt (str): The raw text prompt. * model (str): Target Anthropic model. * effort (str | None): Normalized effort level. * max_tokens (int): Sized output token budget.

Returns: * tuple[dict, list[str]]: A 2-tuple containing the parameter dictionary passed to the SDK and the list of beta header strings.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_anthropic implementation
params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, ceiling)
start = time.time()
message = _send(params, betas)

docs.title: _resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Computes the optimal planned output token budget and the maximum context ceiling permissible for the model without exceeding context windows.

Implementation: 

def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (max_tokens, ceiling): the planned budget and the largest budget allowed.

    `prompt_tokens` comes from count_tokens() (already scaled by ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO).
    The ceiling respects the model output cap, the context window (prompt + output +
    ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN — the same margin input_token_budget reserves), and
    ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS when set.
    """
    context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)  # same value input_token_budget reserved

    room = max(context_window - prompt_tokens - ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096)
    ceiling = min(output_cap, room, cap) if cap else min(output_cap, room)
    if ceiling < wanted:
        # Small shortfalls (template overhead on a budget-packed prompt) are expected; only report real cuts.
        if ceiling < wanted * 0.9:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED", wanted=f"{wanted:,}", available=f"{ceiling:,}")
        wanted = ceiling
    return wanted, ceiling
The helper determines the context window and output capacity via get_model_limits(). It computes the remaining available space (room) after subtracting prompt tokens and safety margin (ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN). The hard ceiling is clamped by the model's physical output cap, available room, and any user cap defined by ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. If ceiling falls below the planned output budget (wanted), the budget is clamped, emitting a WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED warning if reduced by more than 10%.

Parameters: * prompt_tokens (int): Tokenized length of the prompt, pre-scaled by token ratios. * model (str): Target model name. * effort (str | None): Normalized reasoning effort.

Returns: * tuple[int, int]: A 2-tuple representing (max_tokens, ceiling).

Example: 

# Extracted from call_anthropic implementation
raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
max_tokens, ceiling = _resolve_max_tokens(int(raw_tokens * get_token_ratio()), model, effort)
params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, max_tokens)

docs.title: _stream_message()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]) -> anthropic.types.Message:

Description: Dispatches a streaming request over the Anthropic client and blocks until the stream completes, returning the finalized Message object.

Implementation: 

def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    client = _get_client()
    if betas:
        with client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params) as stream:
            return stream.get_final_message()
    with client.messages.stream(**params) as stream:
        return stream.get_final_message()
The function retrieves the client singleton and branches based on whether beta headers are present. If betas are provided, it invokes client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params). Otherwise, it invokes client.messages.stream(**params). The context manager blocks until the full message is received, returning stream.get_final_message().

Parameters: * params (dict): The payload dictionary of API parameters. * betas (list[str]): List of active Anthropic beta feature strings.

Returns: * anthropic.types.Message: The finalized message response from Claude.

Example: 

# Extracted from _send implementation
try:
    return _stream_message(params, betas)
except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
    # ...

docs.title: _fallback_rejected()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:

Description: Inspects an API 400 BadRequestError message to determine whether the failure was caused by server-side fallback incompatibility rather than invalid user input.

Implementation: 

def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:
    """True when a 400 rejects the fallback feature itself (beta header not enabled, or
    `fallbacks: "default"` unsupported for this model/account) — not a user config error."""
    text = error_text.lower()
    if "anthropic-beta" in text and "server-side-fallback" in text:
        return True
    return params.get("extra_body", {}).get("fallbacks") == "default" and "fallbacks" in text
Evaluates whether the error string references beta header rejection ("anthropic-beta" and "server-side-fallback") or indicates that "fallbacks": "default" is unsupported on the account. Returns True to authorize an automated recovery attempt without fallbacks.

Parameters: * error_text (str): Lowercased exception error message. * params (dict): The parameter dictionary passed into the failed request.

Returns: * bool: True if the fallback header caused the 400 rejection; otherwise False.

Example: 

# Extracted from _send implementation
except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
    if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
        _fallbacks_disabled = True
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
        retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
        return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
    raise

docs.title: _send()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]) -> anthropic.types.Message:

Description: Sends a single streamed request to Claude. If the Anthropic API rejects the fallback configuration with an HTTP 400, it disables fallbacks for the process run and retries without fallback arguments.

Implementation: 

def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    """Send one streamed request; disable fallbacks for the run if the feature is unavailable."""
    global _fallbacks_disabled
    try:
        return _stream_message(params, betas)
    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise
Executes _stream_message(params, betas). If an anthropic.BadRequestError is raised, it checks _fallback_rejected(). When verified, the global _fallbacks_disabled flag is flipped to True, a WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED warning event is emitted, and the request is immediately retried without extra_body or beta headers. Unrelated errors are re-raised.

Parameters: * params (dict): Parameter dictionary for the request. * betas (list[str]): Beta header strings.

Returns: * anthropic.types.Message: The finalized message response.

Raises: * anthropic.BadRequestError: If the request fails for reasons unrelated to fallback compatibility.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_anthropic implementation
start = time.time()
message = _send(params, betas)
if message.stop_reason == "max_tokens" and max_tokens < ceiling:
    # ...

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated USD cost of an inference call based on token consumption, prompt cache read/write hits, and pricing tables matched via longest model prefix.

Implementation: 

def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:
    price = next((_PRICING[k] for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if (model or "").startswith(k)), None)
    if price is None:
        return None
    p_in, p_out, p_read = price
    return (tokens_in * p_in + tokens_out * p_out + cache_read * p_read + cache_write * p_in * 1.25) / 1_000_000
Matches model against keys in _PRICING sorted in descending order of length to ensure specialized sub-variants match before base models. Multiplies input, output, cache-read, and cache-creation tokens by their million-token rate (evaluating 5-minute cache writes at $1.25\times$ base input cost) and returns the total cost in USD. Returns None if the model has no entry in the pricing table.

Parameters: * model (str): Served model name. * tokens_in (int): Count of non-cached prompt input tokens. * tokens_out (int): Count of generated output tokens. * cache_read (int): Count of tokens read from Anthropic prompt cache. * cache_write (int): Count of tokens written to Anthropic prompt cache.

Returns: * float | None: Total USD expenditure, or None if unknown.

Example: 

# Extracted from _message_cost implementation
if message.stop_reason == "refusal" and not _extract_text(message):
    return 0.0  # declined before any output: not billed
return _price(served_model, *_tokens(message.usage))

docs.title: _tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _tokens(usage: object) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:

Description: Safely extracts token count metrics from an Anthropic message usage object.

Implementation: 

def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    return (
        getattr(usage, "input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
    )
Uses getattr to safely retrieve input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, and cache_creation_input_tokens from SDK usage structures, defaulting missing attributes or None values to 0.

Parameters: * usage (object): The usage attribute of an Anthropic message or iteration block.

Returns: * tuple[int, int, int, int]: A 4-tuple of (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read, cache_write).

Example: 

# Extracted from _record_usage implementation
served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(message.usage)
cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)

docs.title: _message_cost()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _message_cost(message: anthropic.types.Message, served_model: str) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the comprehensive cost of a completed message, iterating through multiple fallback attempt blocks if present or zeroing out unbilled refusals.

Implementation: 

def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:
    """Estimated USD cost of one response. With server-side fallbacks, usage.iterations holds the
    per-attempt usage (each billed at its own model's rate; an attempt declined before any output is
    unbilled); top-level usage covers only the attempt that produced the returned message."""
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        total, known = 0.0, True
        for entry in iterations:
            tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(entry)
            if tokens_out == 0:
                continue  # declined before any output (primary or fallback attempt): not billed
            cost = _price(getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write)
            known = known and cost is not None
            total += cost or 0.0
        return total if known else None
    if message.stop_reason == "refusal" and not _extract_text(message):
        return 0.0  # declined before any output: not billed
    return _price(served_model, *_tokens(message.usage))
When server-side fallbacks are invoked, message.usage.iterations captures token metrics per attempt. The helper walks each iteration, skipping attempts that produced zero output tokens (which Anthropic does not bill), resolving prices based on each attempt's specific model rate. If iterations are absent and the model immediately refused without generating text, cost is evaluated as $0.00. Otherwise, top-level usage is computed via _price().

Parameters: * message (anthropic.types.Message): The completed message object. * served_model (str): Identifier of the model that generated the final response.

Returns: * float | None: Total cost in USD, or None if unknown.

Example: 

# Extracted from _record_usage implementation
served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(message.usage)
cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)
record_usage(
    "ANTHROPIC", served_model, input_tokens=tokens_in, output_tokens=tokens_out, cache_read=cache_read, cache_write=cache_write, cost=cost
)

docs.title: _record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _record_usage(message: anthropic.types.Message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float) -> None:

Description: Updates global usage tracking and outputs diagnostic log telemetry, comparing observed Claude token counts against raw estimates to evaluate token ratio scaling.

Implementation: 

def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float) -> None:
    served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
    tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(message.usage)
    cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)
    record_usage(
        "ANTHROPIC", served_model, input_tokens=tokens_in, output_tokens=tokens_out, cache_read=cache_read, cache_write=cache_write, cost=cost
    )

    # Observed Claude/tiktoken ratio helps tune ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO for this codebase.
    ratio = (tokens_in + cache_read + cache_write) / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"ANTHROPIC USAGE | model={served_model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | stop={message.stop_reason} | "
        f"in={tokens_in:,} | out={tokens_out:,} | cache_read={cache_read:,} | cache_write={cache_write:,} | "
        f"est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
The helper extracts token counts and cost estimates, logging them to the centralized accumulator via record_usage(). It computes an observed token expansion ratio by dividing total prompt tokens by raw_prompt_tokens. This metric is logged alongside elapsed execution time and stop reasons to aid in tuning the ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO configuration.

Parameters: * message (anthropic.types.Message): The received response message. * raw_prompt_tokens (int): Initial unscaled prompt token count. * effort (str | None): Active reasoning effort. * elapsed (float): Total request round-trip time in seconds.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_anthropic implementation
_record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start)
if is_debug():
    _log_thinking(message)

docs.title: _log_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _log_thinking(message: anthropic.types.Message) -> None:

Description: Extracts thinking content blocks from the message payload and writes their reasoning summaries to the debug log file.

Implementation: 

def _log_thinking(message) -> None:
    for block in message.content:
        if getattr(block, "type", None) == "thinking" and getattr(block, "thinking", ""):
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{block.thinking}", dest="LOG")
The function scans message.content for blocks with type == "thinking". When found, their text content is emitted to log destinations via emit_raw(..., dest="LOG"), ensuring intermediate model reasoning is captured without polluting stdout.

Parameters: * message (anthropic.types.Message): The completed response message.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_anthropic implementation
_record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start)
if is_debug():
    _log_thinking(message)

docs.title: _served_by_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _served_by_fallback(message: anthropic.types.Message) -> bool:

Description: Inspects content blocks and iteration structures to determine if the returned response was generated by a server-side fallback model rather than the primary model.

Implementation: 

def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:
    if any(getattr(block, "type", None) == "fallback" for block in message.content):
        return True
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    return any(getattr(entry, "type", None) == "fallback_message" for entry in iterations)
Returns True if any block in message.content has type == "fallback" or if any entry within message.usage.iterations is marked with type == "fallback_message".

Parameters: * message (anthropic.types.Message): The received response message.

Returns: * bool: True if a fallback model served the request; otherwise False.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_anthropic implementation
if _served_by_fallback(message) and message.stop_reason != "refusal":
    count_event("ANTHROPIC", "fallbacks")
    emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_SERVED", model=model, served_by=getattr(message, "model", "unknown"))

docs.title: _extract_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _extract_text(message: anthropic.types.Message) -> str:

Description: Concatenates and returns all text segments found within the message's content blocks.

Implementation: 

def _extract_text(message) -> str:
    return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text")
Iterates through message.content, filtering for blocks where type == "text", and joins their text fields into a unified string. Thinking blocks and fallback markers are excluded.

Parameters: * message (anthropic.types.Message): The completed response message.

Returns: * str: Joined response text.

Example: 

# Extracted from call_anthropic implementation
text = _extract_text(message)
if message.stop_reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS:
    count_event("ANTHROPIC", "truncations")
    emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED", max_tokens=f"{params['max_tokens']:,}")
    return TruncatedResponse(text)

docs.title: Data Structures
docs.text: The module relies on structured pricing, configuration limits, and custom container objects to govern token allocations and error handling.

docs.title: _PRICING
docs.text:
Static dictionary mapping model identifier prefixes to their USD rates per one million tokens. Rates are represented as a 3-tuple of floats: (input_price, output_price, cache_read_price). Cache creation writes are computed as $1.25\times$ input price.

Model Prefix Input Price ($ / 1M) Output Price ($ / 1M) Cache Read Price ($ / 1M) claude-opus-5-5 4.00 20.00 0.20 claude-opus-5 5.00 25.00 0.50 claude-fable-5-1 10.00 50.00 0.25 claude-fable-5 10.00 50.00 1.00 claude-mythos-5-1 10.00 50.00 0.25 claude-mythos-5 10.00 50.00 1.00 claude-sonnet-5 2.00 10.00 0.20 claude-opus-4-8 5.00 25.00 0.50 claude-opus-4-7 5.00 25.00 0.50 claude-opus-4-6 5.00 25.00 0.50 claude-sonnet-4-6 3.00 15.00 0.30 claude-haiku-4-5 1.00 5.00 0.10

docs.text:
Static fallback definitions used when dynamic retrieval from the Anthropic Models API fails.

Constant Value Description _MODEL_LIMITS["claude-haiku-4-5"] (200_000, 64_000) 200K context window, 64K maximum output tokens _DEFAULT_LIMITS (1_000_000, 128_000) Baseline default: 1M context window, 128K maximum output tokens

docs.title: Model Request Schema (params)
docs.text:
Dictionary constructed by _build_request() and passed to the Anthropic Messages streaming API.

Field Type Description model str Model identifier (e.g., "claude-sonnet-5"). max_tokens int Sized output token budget. messages list[dict[str, str]] Single user turn: [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]. thinking dict[str, str] (Optional) Adaptive config {"type": "adaptive"} or explicit budget {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N}. output_config dict[str, str] (Optional) Effort level mapping {"effort": effort} for adaptive models. cache_control dict[str, str] (Optional) Ephemeral caching marker {"type": "ephemeral"} when enabled. extra_body dict[str, Any] (Optional) Fallback configuration dictionary (e.g., {"fallbacks": "default"}).

docs.title: Fallback Configuration Return Shape
docs.text:
Structured 2-tuple returned by _fallback_config(model).

Index Type Description 0 list[str] Beta header flags (e.g., ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"] or []). 1 dict Extra body arguments containing the fallback specification or {}.

docs.title: Token Accounting Quadruple
docs.text:
Structured 4-tuple returned by _tokens(usage).

Index Field Type Description 0 tokens_in int Total prompt input tokens (excluding cache read). 1 tokens_out int Total generated output tokens. 2 cache_read int Input tokens resolved from cache. 3 cache_write int Input tokens written to cache creation.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The module provides defensive recovery mechanisms to manage safety refusals, token truncation, network timeouts, and rejected beta headers:

docs.title: 1. Refusal Exception Escalation
docs.text: When Claude's internal safety classifiers decline to respond, the API assigns message.stop_reason = "refusal". The driver extracts the category string from message.stop_details (if present), logs a WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL warning, increments the provider refusal counter via count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals"), and raises an LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC"). Upstream orchestrators in call_llm.py trap this error to memoize the failure in cache storage and prevent repeated billing.

docs.title: 2. Output Budget Truncation and Retry Loop
docs.text: If a response stops with message.stop_reason == "max_tokens" and the initial max_tokens allocation was below the maximum context ceiling, the driver automatically attempts a recovery. It records the first attempt's token usage, emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY, rebuilds the request parameters with max_tokens = ceiling, and streams a second attempt. If the second attempt still terminates with a truncation stop reason ("max_tokens" or "model_context_window_exceeded"), it wraps the extracted text in a TruncatedResponse container. Upstream cache handlers check for isinstance(result, TruncatedResponse) to avoid caching truncated text.

docs.title: 3. Server-Side Fallback Rejection Recovery
docs.text:
Certain API accounts or models may reject server-side fallback configurations. When _send() encounters an anthropic.BadRequestError, it calls _fallback_rejected(str(e), params): 

    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise
If the error indicates that the fallback beta header or payload was rejected, _fallbacks_disabled is set to True to protect subsequent calls in the run. The current request is immediately retried without fallback parameters.

docs.title: 4. Models API Fallback Protection
docs.text: During model limits resolution in get_model_limits(), network errors or permission boundaries can cause client.models.retrieve() to throw an anthropic.APIError. The module catches this error, emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP, and falls back to static definitions in _MODEL_LIMITS or _DEFAULT_LIMITS, ensuring pipeline execution continues even when offline or behind restrictive firewalls.

docs.title: llm_common.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_common.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the vendor-specific transport and parsing mechanics established in llm_anthropic.py, the llm_common.py module defines the shared, provider-agnostic domain layer for the entire inference pipeline. It operates as a zero-dependency foundational component that explicitly avoids importing third-party provider SDKs (anthropic, google-genai, openai). By establishing uniform domain representations for incomplete generations, provider rejections, runtime deduplication, and financial telemetry, it isolates the high-level orchestration workflows in call_llm.py from the underlying provider implementations.

The primary architectural role of llm_common.py is to manage stateful inference invariants across multi-step execution graphs. It provides a circuit-breaking refusal memoization mechanism (_refused) that prevents wasteful network retries against models that deterministically decline prompts due to safety, moderation, or policy violations. Furthermore, it defines custom string subtype semantics (TruncatedResponse) to intercept length-truncated completions before they can contaminate the disk-backed cache in call_llm.py, while simultaneously offering a centralized session ledger (_usage) to record token volumes, thinking token allocations, prompt cache interactions, and accumulated operational costs.

    end

docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class TruncatedResponse(str):

Description: A specialized string subclass that tags model responses truncated by output token limits or context window boundaries. It preserves standard string behavior across serialization and downstream logging operations while exposing a sentinel truncated = True attribute. Higher-level orchestration layers, specifically call_llm and parse_yaml_response, inspect this boolean attribute to bypass persistent disk caching and signal upstream node retries.

Attributes: * truncated (bool): Sentinel flag, always set to True, identifying the output buffer as incomplete.

Example: 

class TruncatedResponse(str):
    """Response text from a reply that was cut off; call_llm returns it but never caches it."""

    truncated = True
The implementation derives directly from native str without mutating base string memory layouts. Because instances pass standard string type checks throughout the Python runtime, intermediate formatters can safely inspect, print, or measure the truncated payload without raising type errors. Upstream orchestrators use getattr(response, "truncated", False) to selectively invalidate the run from the persistence cache, ensuring that defective, half-formed YAML blocks or code generations are forced through subsequent re-sampling passes.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError): def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):

Description: Domain exception raised when an LLM provider declines to generate a completion due to content moderation filters, safety guardrails, or recitation protections. It encapsulates the originating provider, model identifier, refusal classification category, and a criticality flag (retryable). This flag differentiates between deterministic prompt declines (such as system-level policy blocks that must never be re-sent) and stochastic candidate blocks (such as mid-generation recitation triggers that may succeed upon re-sampling).

Parameters: * model (str): The specific model identifier that issued the refusal (e.g., "claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219"). * category (str | None): The provider's safety category code or rejection reason (e.g., "safety", "recitation", "content_filter"). * provider (str): The identifier of the rejecting vendor platform. Defaults to "ANTHROPIC". * retryable (bool): Indicates whether repeating the inference request with alternative sampling parameters could succeed. Defaults to False.

Returns: * LLMRefusalError: Instantiated exception object with formatted diagnostic details.

Raises: * N/A: Instantiation does not raise errors.

Example: 

class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the provider (and any configured fallback) declines a request.

    retryable=False: the same request is declined again (Claude refusal, blocked prompt,
    prohibited content) — call_llm remembers it and does not re-send it on node retries.
    retryable=True: an output-side block that a new sample can pass (Gemini RECITATION / OTHER /
    SAFETY on the candidate, OpenRouter content_filter) — node retries re-sample normally.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):
        self.model = model
        self.category = category
        self.provider = provider
        self.retryable = retryable
        super().__init__(f"{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category or 'unknown'})")
The constructor structures diagnostic messages uniformly across diverse provider payloads, converting ambiguous vendor error codes into a standardized runtime exception. Downstream dispatchers evaluate the instance's retryable property to modulate retry loops. If retryable evaluates to False, the refusal is committed to the module's internal lookup table, short-circuiting identical subsequent requests before invoking network sockets.

docs.title: request_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:

Description: Generates a deterministic SHA-256 hexadecimal hash identifying an inference request. The key is composed of a scoped header containing the provider name, the model string, and the normalized reasoning effort level, followed by the exact prompt payload. This hash serves as the primary indexing key for refusal tracking and cache deduplication.

Parameters: * provider (str): The upstream inference provider (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER"). * model (str): The target model name string. * thinking_level (str | None): The configured reasoning intensity (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"), or None if operating without reasoning tokens. * prompt (str): The complete serialized prompt string passed to the driver.

Returns: * str: A 64-character lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal digest representing the request signature.

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
The implementation uses a delimiter-separated scope prefix (provider|model|thinking_level\n) to ensure that identical prompt strings routed to different models or distinct reasoning budgets yield collision-free digests. The resulting string is encoded into UTF-8 before being passed to hashlib.sha256. This mechanism provides an identical hash output across diverse operating systems and process lifecycles.

docs.title: remember_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:

Description: Registers an encountered non-retryable LLMRefusalError into the module-level refusal registry (_refused), binding the error object to the request's deterministic SHA-256 hash.

Parameters: * key (str): The hexadecimal request digest computed via request_key(). * error (LLMRefusalError): The refusal error instance capturing the failure context.

Returns: * None

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:
    _refused[key] = error
This function populates the private global dictionary _refused to provide process-level memorization of declined inference attempts. When synthesis nodes attempt retries following a fatal safety refusal, registering the error through this function allows the caller to break out of cascading execution cycles immediately. The stored error retains its original stack context, failure model, and safety categories for subsequent inspection.

docs.title: previous_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:

Description: Queries the module-level refusal registry for a previously recorded LLMRefusalError matching the provided request hash.

Parameters: * key (str): The hexadecimal request digest computed via request_key().

Returns: * LLMRefusalError | None: The cached refusal error if previously recorded; otherwise None.

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:
    return _refused.get(key)
The retrieval helper executes an $O(1)$ dictionary lookup against the _refused table. Orchestrators in call_llm evaluate this lookup before calculating token bounds or initiating network requests. If an error is returned, the orchestrator immediately raises the memorized exception, preventing unnecessary network traffic, API quota consumption, and unneeded billing on inputs that will reliably trigger safety filters.

docs.title: record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def record_usage(provider: str, model: str, *, input_tokens: int = 0, output_tokens: int = 0, thinking_tokens: int = 0, cache_read: int = 0, cache_write: int = 0, cost: float | None = None) -> None:

Description: Records token volumes, prompt cache mechanics, and operational expenses for a completed inference call into the global usage ledger (_usage). It aggregates metrics per provider, tracks unique models utilized, and updates cost flags based on pricing availability.

Parameters: * provider (str): The provider identifier (e.g., "GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC"). * model (str): The specific model used for the completion. * input_tokens (int): Count of prompt/input tokens processed. Defaults to 0. * output_tokens (int): Count of total output tokens generated, including thinking tokens. Defaults to 0. * thinking_tokens (int): Subset of output tokens dedicated to internal model reasoning. Defaults to 0. * cache_read (int): Count of input tokens read from the provider's prompt cache. Defaults to 0. * cache_write (int): Count of input tokens written to create new prompt cache entries. Defaults to 0. * cost (float | None): Financial cost in USD for the transaction. If passed as None, marks the provider's overall cost as uncomputable. Defaults to None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Accumulate one call. `output_tokens` includes thinking; `thinking_tokens` is the reported subset.
    `cost` is USD; None means the price is unknown for this model (summary shows n/a)."""
    entry = _usage.setdefault(
        provider,
        {
            "models": set(),
            "calls": 0,
            "input": 0,
            "output": 0,
            "thinking": 0,
            "cache_read": 0,
            "cache_write": 0,
            "cost": 0.0,
            "cost_known": True,
            "refusals": 0,
            "fallbacks": 0,
            "truncations": 0,
        },
    )
    if model:
        entry["models"].add(model)
    entry["calls"] += 1
    entry["input"] += input_tokens or 0
    entry["output"] += output_tokens or 0
    entry["thinking"] += thinking_tokens or 0
    entry["cache_read"] += cache_read or 0
    entry["cache_write"] += cache_write or 0
    if cost is None:
        entry["cost_known"] = False
    else:
        entry["cost"] += cost
The implementation uses dict.setdefault to initialize zeroed usage buckets on the first call for a given provider. Integer token metrics defensively fall back to 0 if passed falsy or None values. When tracking costs, if any call for a model lacks price metadata (cost is None), the ledger sets cost_known to False, signaling downstream reporting routines in output.py to render costs as unknown (n/a) rather than misleadingly incomplete figures.

docs.title: count_event()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:

Description: Increments discrete operational anomaly counters ("refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations") for a specified provider entry within the global usage ledger.

Parameters: * provider (str): The target provider key in the usage ledger. * event (str): The metric counter to increment; expected to be one of "refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations".

Returns: * None

Raises: * KeyError: If event does not match an existing key in the ledger entry template.

Example: 

def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:
    """Increment 'refusals' | 'fallbacks' | 'truncations' for a provider."""
    entry = _usage.setdefault(
        provider,
        {
            "models": set(),
            "calls": 0,
            "input": 0,
            "output": 0,
            "thinking": 0,
            "cache_read": 0,
            "cache_write": 0,
            "cost": 0.0,
            "cost_known": True,
            "refusals": 0,
            "fallbacks": 0,
            "truncations": 0,
        },
    )
    entry[event] += 1
This function maintains parity between token volume reporting and pipeline operational health. By sharing the initialization structure with record_usage(), it allows events to be recorded before any tokens have been successfully generated—such as during immediate prompt rejections or connection fallback events. Upstream adapters call this helper whenever fallback headers are disabled, responses are truncated at context limits, or refusals are intercepted.

docs.title: get_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_usage_summary() -> dict:

Description: Generates a consolidated summary of token allocations, costs, and operational events for all providers that processed at least one call during the execution run. Transforms internal sets of model names into lexicographically sorted lists.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary mapping provider names to shallow-copied usage records with sorted "models" lists, omitting inactive providers.

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def get_usage_summary() -> dict:
    """{provider: totals} for every provider that made at least one call this run."""
    return {provider: dict(entry, models=sorted(entry["models"])) for provider, entry in _usage.items() if entry["calls"]}
The summary pipeline uses a dictionary comprehension that filters out uncalled providers (if entry["calls"]). It creates a decoupled copy of the internal accumulator using dict(entry, ...), explicitly converting the internal set of model names into a deterministically sorted list. This transformation guarantees stable rendering when generating tables or serialized CLI output summaries.

docs.title: reset_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def reset_usage() -> None:

Description: Resets all in-memory usage ledgers and refusal caches, returning the module to an uninitialized state. Primarily intended for automated test suites and isolated execution resets.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def reset_usage() -> None:
    _usage.clear()
    _refused.clear()
The helper invokes .clear() on both the _usage ledger and _refused map in-place. This guarantees that subsequent pipeline executions within the same Python process boundary do not retain dirty telemetry or memorized refusals from previous test runs.

docs.title: warn_once()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a warning signature has already been displayed during the active process run, tracking compound keys to prevent noisy CLI log duplication.

Parameters: * key (str): The primary category or message identifier. * *parts (Any): Optional additional hashable values (such as model names or HTTP status codes) forming a composite warning key.

Returns: * bool: True if this specific warning marker is encountered for the first time; False if it has already been registered.

Raises: * N/A.

Example: 

def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:
    """True the first time a (key, parts) combination is seen this run."""
    marker = (key, *parts)
    if marker in _warned:
        return False
    _warned.add(marker)
    return True
The helper constructs a tuple (key, *parts) to serve as a composite hash in the private _warned set. If the marker is already present, the function returns False, allowing caller logging blocks to exit early. When a new marker is encountered, it is recorded in the set and returns True, ensuring that identical warnings (e.g., deprecated parameters, unsupported reasoning flags) are emitted only once per session.

docs.title: Internal Helpers
docs.text:
The utils/llm_common.py module maintains three internal, process-scoped data containers to track runtime state without exposing mutable data structures directly to external modules.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refused-request memo: a declined prompt is declined again, so PocketFlow retries
# must not re-send it (wasted rate limit, and billed partial output on mid-stream declines).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_refused = {}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Usage ledger (one per process; a run is sequential)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_usage = {}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# De-duplicated warnings
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_warned = set()

docs.title: _refused
docs.text: A process-level dictionary (dict[str, LLMRefusalError]) that maps SHA-256 request signatures generated by request_key() to their corresponding LLMRefusalError instances. It acts as an in-memory cache to prevent repetitive, non-retryable API calls. External modules access this dictionary exclusively through remember_refusal(), previous_refusal(), and reset_usage().

docs.title: _usage
docs.text: A process-level dictionary (dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) that aggregates operational statistics and token accounting across all active LLM providers. Each entry stores call counts, token usage, cost data, and error metrics. State modifications and reads are restricted to record_usage(), count_event(), get_usage_summary(), and reset_usage().

docs.title: _warned
docs.text: A process-level set (set[tuple[str, ...]]) containing composite warning markers. It records unique tuples passed to warn_once() to deduplicate warning messages in CLI logs throughout the life of the process.

docs.title: UsageRecord Schema
docs.text:
The internal dictionary structure maintained for each provider inside the _usage ledger, and exposed in shallow-copied form via get_usage_summary().

Field Type Description models set[str] (internal) / list[str] (summary) Unique model identifiers invoked for this provider during the run. calls int Total number of attempted inference calls dispatched. input int Total count of input/prompt tokens processed. output int Total count of output tokens generated (including thinking tokens). thinking int Subset of output tokens dedicated to model reasoning/thinking. cache_read int Prompt tokens retrieved directly from provider-side caches. cache_write int Prompt tokens written to create new provider-side cache entries. cost float Cumulative calculated cost in USD across all calls. cost_known bool Flag indicating whether all models used have known pricing metadata (False if any model cost was None). refusals int Count of declined requests encountered for this provider. fallbacks int Count of times the provider dropped down to secondary models or disabled fallback beta headers. truncations int Count of model completions cut off by context or token limits.

docs.title: RefusalMemo Schema
docs.text:
The schema mapping maintained by the _refused dictionary for recording declined requests.

Key Value Type Description SHA-256 digest string (64 characters) LLMRefusalError The captured refusal error instance, preserving model, category, provider, and retryability semantics.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module provides the foundation for error handling across the system's inference layers:

  • Refusal Classification: LLMRefusalError introduces a structured categorization for declined prompts. By dividing errors into retryable=False (fatal declines, policy triggers, deterministic refusals) and retryable=True (transient safety blocks, recitation checks on output candidates), it provides the decision logic necessary for upstream graph nodes to either resample or abandon execution paths.
  • Truncation Signatures: Rather than raising an unhandled exception upon encountering context window limits or maximum token exhaustion, the module provides TruncatedResponse. This string subtype allows pipelines to inspect partial completions, bypass the disk-based cache, and trigger controlled retries via higher-level handlers (such as YAML parsers).
  • Cost Incompleteness Guard: If an invoked model does not have pricing metrics available, record_usage() flags cost_known = False. This prevents the pipeline from displaying inaccurate or partially calculated cost summaries in terminal logs.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• call_llm.py — Central inference dispatcher that uses request_key, previous_refusal, remember_refusal, and TruncatedResponse to govern caching and execution.
  • llm_anthropic.py — Anthropic integration driver that translates API response metrics into record_usage and handles LLMRefusalError and TruncatedResponse.
  • llm_gemini.py — Google Gemini adapter that reports token usage and converts candidate safety blocks into LLMRefusalError.
  • llm_openrouter.py — OpenRouter integration layer that reports multi-provider costs and usage to record_usage.
  • output.py — Telemetry and console formatting layer that processes get_usage_summary() to render final execution tables.

docs.title: llm_config.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/llm_config.py

Following the foundational telemetry and state-tracking mechanisms defined in utils/llm_common.py, the utils/llm_config.py module establishes the centralized configuration, authentication preflight, and context-length resolution engine for the entire codebase.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/llm_config.py module acts as the authoritative source of truth for provider resolution, model identification, token budgeting, and environment preflight verification across the system. It was extracted from utils/call_llm.py to decouple the cyclic dependency loop previously binding call_llm and utils/token_utils.py. Upstream pipeline entry points—including main.py, utils/call_llm.py, and utils/token_utils.py—consume this module to resolve active provider configurations, query context window boundaries, and validate SDK credentials before initiating expensive pipeline traversals.

The module manages multi-provider configuration mechanics for Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini (via both Vertex AI and Google AI Studio), and OpenRouter gateway endpoints. It normalizes provider-specific model strings, resolves API endpoints, sets default token margins, and harmonizes model-specific reasoning controls. Additionally, it contains the credential preflight engine that verifies SDK installations, parses local OAuth sessions, queries local credential directories, and checks Workload Identity Federation configs to guarantee early failure reporting prior to pipeline execution.

docs.title: anthropic_output_cap()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:

Description: Resolves the user-configured ceiling for Anthropic token generation by inspecting the ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable. It parses the numeric value using _env_int, returning None if the environment variable is not defined or is not a positive integer.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * int | None: The parsed upper bound integer token count, or None if unset or invalid.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:
    """ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS as an int, or None when unset/invalid."""
    return _env_int("ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")

The function reads the environment through the internal helper _env_int, which strips whitespace and confirms the presence of positive numeric digits. This ensures that misconfigured strings (such as negative numbers or non-numeric characters) do not trigger runtime conversion errors in downstream token budgeting calculations. By returning None in the absence of an explicit cap, it allows adaptive and legacy models to default to their respective preset limits.

docs.title: anthropic_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Calculates the target output token allocation for adaptive Claude models based on the requested thinking effort level. The value is looked up from ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT and clamped by anthropic_output_cap() if an explicit system ceiling is enforced.

Parameters: * thinking_level (str | None): The requested thinking effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"), or None for default.

Returns: * int: The computed output token budget clamped to the active system ceiling.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-effort table value capped by ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (adaptive models)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

This function normalizes the input effort string to lowercase and retrieves the planned token count from ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT. If an unknown or empty effort level is passed, it falls back to the default None key entry (64_000 tokens). The resulting integer is then compared against anthropic_output_cap(), returning the lower of the two values to guarantee compliance with user-defined resource constraints.

docs.title: anthropic_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Normalizes and validates the specified thinking level into an effort string supported by the target Anthropic model family. It maps unsupported low-tier values (e.g., "minimal") up to "low", downgrades "xhigh" to "high" for older Claude 4.6 models that predate extended thinking, and drops unrecognized levels to None.

Parameters: * model (str): Target Anthropic model name or identifier. * level (str | None): Proposed thinking effort level.

Returns: * str | None: The normalized effort string accepted by the Anthropic API, or None to adopt the model's default reasoning behavior.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Thinking level → effort the model accepts: minimal → low, xhigh → high on the 4.6 family,
    unknown values → None (model default)."""
    if not level:
        return None
    level = level.lower()
    if level == "minimal":
        level = "low"
    if level not in ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS:
        return None
    if level == "xhigh" and (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES):
        return "high"
    return level

The normalization pipeline guarantees that model-specific API constraints are satisfied before dispatch. The Anthropic API does not offer a "minimal" effort category, so the function maps it directly to "low". Furthermore, because models matching ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES (such as claude-opus-4-6 and claude-sonnet-4-6) reject the "xhigh" parameter with an HTTP 400 bad request, the function transparently steps down "xhigh" requests to "high" for those specific identifiers.

docs.title: anthropic_planned_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Computes the planned output token reservation for an Anthropic request before context window ceilings are applied. It routes adaptive models to anthropic_output_budget and pre-adaptive models (such as Claude Haiku 4.5) to a composite formula combining budget tokens with a fixed reply token allowance.

Parameters: * model (str): The target Anthropic model identifier. * thinking_level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort string.

Returns: * int: Total output tokens planned for the request, clamped by ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Claude max_tokens the request will plan for (before the model/context ceiling): the per-effort
    table on adaptive models, budget_tokens + 16K on pre-adaptive ones (Haiku 4.5), capped by
    ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Shared by llm_anthropic and token_utils.input_token_budget."""
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, thinking_level)
    if (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
        return anthropic_output_budget(effort)
    planned = ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL.get(effort, 0) + ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(planned, cap) if cap else planned

The function identifies whether the model belongs to the modern adaptive thinking family via ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES. For adaptive architectures, output allocations are derived from anthropic_output_budget(). For pre-adaptive variants, the function calculates the sum of the thinking budget from ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL and ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS (16_000), ensuring that the token planning phase leaves sufficient headroom for completion generation.

docs.title: gemini_thinking_mode()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:

Description: Determines the reasoning mode and valid configuration boundaries supported by a specified Gemini model. Distinguishes between modern Gemini 3.x categorical levels, legacy Gemini 2.5 numeric budget ranges, and non-reasoning architectures.

Parameters: * model (str): Target Gemini model name or path.

Returns: * tuple[str, object]: A two-element tuple consisting of: 1. Mode identifier string: "level", "budget", or "none". 2. Specification payload: a tuple of allowed level strings for "level", a 3-tuple (min, max, can_disable) for "budget", or None for "none".

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """('level', allowed_levels) for Gemini 3.x, ('budget', (min, max, can_disable)) for 2.5,
    ('none', None) for models without a thinking control the project maps."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, low, high, can_disable in GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "budget", (low, high, can_disable)
    if not name.startswith("gemini-") or name.startswith(("gemini-1", "gemini-2")):
        return "none", None  # 1.x / 2.0, other 2.5 variants (image, live, TTS) and non-Gemini ids
    for prefix, levels in GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "level", levels
    # Other 3.x ids, '-latest' aliases (gemini-flash-latest, gemini-pro-latest) and newer families:
    # the level set every documented 3.x model accepts (a model that rejects it is handled at runtime).
    return "level", GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS

The function strips namespace prefixes using gemini_model_id() to extract the core model name. It matches the name against GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES to determine if legacy budget-based reasoning applies. For non-reasoning legacy models (gemini-1*, gemini-2.0*), it returns ("none", None). For Gemini 3.x and modern variants, it checks GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS using longest-prefix semantics, falling back to GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS for unrecognized modern versions or rolling aliases.

docs.title: gemini_model_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes resource names and API paths by stripping directory qualifiers, publisher namespaces, and whitespace.

Parameters: * model (str): Fully-qualified or relative model path (e.g., "publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash").

Returns: * str: The bare lowercased model identifier (e.g., "gemini-3.8-flash").

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:
    """'models/gemini-3.8-flash' / 'publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash' → 'gemini-3.8-flash'."""
    return (model or "").strip().lower().rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

This helper sanitizes complex Gemini model references originating from Vertex AI resource identifiers or Google AI Studio endpoints. It performs whitespace stripping, converts characters to lowercase, and splits along forward slashes via rsplit("/", 1)[-1] to isolate the trailing model slug.

docs.title: gemini_vertex_locations()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:

Description: Identifies the valid Google Cloud Vertex AI geographic regions serving a specific Gemini model.

Parameters: * model (str): Target model name or identifier.

Returns: * tuple | None: A tuple of allowed location strings (e.g., ("global", "us")), or None if the model is universally supported across regional endpoints.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:
    """Vertex AI locations that serve a Gemini 3.x model (None = any, including regional endpoints)."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, locations in GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return locations
    return GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS if name.startswith("gemini-3") else None

Because Gemini 3.x preview and production models are served exclusively out of restricted global or multi-region endpoints (such as global, us, or eu) rather than standard default zones like us-central1, this function cross-references the model slug against GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS. If no specific prefix matches, it assigns GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS for any model beginning with "gemini-3", or returns None for unconstrained models.

docs.title: gemini_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:

Description: Resolves the planned output token allocation for Gemini models. Balances thinking level configurations against the model's hard maximum output limit and the GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable.

Parameters: * thinking_level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort string. * output_limit (int | None): The upper output token limit supported by the model, defaulting to GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1] (65_536).

Returns: * int: Planned token generation limit.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:
    """Planned Gemini max_output_tokens: per-level table, capped by the model output limit and
    GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Shared by llm_gemini (request) and token_utils (prompt budget)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    budget = min(budget, output_limit or GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1])
    cap = _env_int("GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

The function queries GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT using the normalized thinking level. It clamps the value against the model's documented output capacity (defaulting to 65,536 tokens if omitted). Finally, it checks for an explicit override via GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, returning the most restrictive token ceiling.

docs.title: openrouter_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Resolves the planned output token budget for models dispatched through OpenRouter. Fetches parameters from the cached OpenRouter model catalog, checks max_completion_tokens, and clamps the result using OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS.

Parameters: * model (str): Target OpenRouter model identifier or slug. * thinking_level (str | None): The requested reasoning intensity.

Returns: * int | None: Planned output tokens, or None if the model cannot be identified in the catalog (signaling that max_tokens should be omitted from the request).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Planned OpenRouter max_tokens: shared per-effort table, capped by the catalog's
    top_provider.max_completion_tokens and OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. None when the model is not
    in the catalog (unknown limits, e.g. a non-OpenRouter proxy): max_tokens is then omitted."""
    info = openrouter_model_info(model)
    if info is None:
        return _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    model_cap = (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("max_completion_tokens")
    budget = min(budget, model_cap) if model_cap else min(budget, 32_000)
    cap = _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

The function looks up model metadata via openrouter_model_info(). If the catalog cannot be retrieved or does not contain the model, it returns the value of OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (which may be None). When catalog metadata is available, it compares the per-effort planned output against top_provider.max_completion_tokens (or a 32,000 token default) and the environment cap.

docs.title: context_output_reserve()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Calculates the number of output tokens that must be subtracted from the total context window to accommodate planned completions and reasoning tokens.

Parameters: * thinking_level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort string.

Returns: * int | None: Token count to reserve from shared context windows (Anthropic and OpenRouter), 0 for architectures with independent input/output buffers (Gemini), or None if unconfigured.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Output tokens that share the context window with the prompt, for the active provider.
    ANTHROPIC / OPENROUTER: the planned max_tokens (thinking included). GEMINI: 0 — Gemini's input and
    output limits are separate. None: the provider does not size output (5% reserve in token_utils)."""
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        return anthropic_planned_output(model, thinking_level)
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        return 0
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return openrouter_output_budget(model, thinking_level)
    return None

Different LLM providers implement distinct context window architectures. Anthropic and OpenRouter share a single context window across input prompts and generated output (including reasoning tokens), requiring the prompt builder to subtract the planned output allocation from the total context limit. In contrast, Google Gemini manages input and output capacities independently, allowing this function to return 0 and make the entire context window available for input prompts.

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Evaluates environment variables to determine the active LLM provider. Gives precedence to LLM_PROVIDER, falls back to detecting Gemini credentials, and avoids auto-selecting Anthropic.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str | None: The normalized provider name in uppercase (e.g., "GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC", "OPENROUTER"), or None if no provider can be resolved.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:
    """Determine the LLM provider from environment variables.

    Explicit LLM_PROVIDER wins; otherwise Gemini credentials select GEMINI (legacy default).
    ANTHROPIC is never auto-selected: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is often exported globally for other
    tools (e.g. Claude Code), and a silent switch to a paid Claude run would be surprising.
    """
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        return provider.strip().upper()
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        return "GEMINI"
    return None

The function enforces safety invariants around automated provider selection. If LLM_PROVIDER is set explicitly, it is normalized to uppercase and returned. Otherwise, it detects GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY to retain legacy backward compatibility. It explicitly avoids auto-selecting ANTHROPIC when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present in the environment, preventing unintentional billing on accounts where CLI tools (such as Claude Code) export credentials globally.

docs.title: gemini_location()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def gemini_location() -> str:

Description: Resolves and lowercases the target Google Cloud Vertex AI geographic location, defaulting to "global".

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: The lowercased target location identifier (e.g., "global", "us", "eu").

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def gemini_location() -> str:
    """GEMINI_LOCATION lower-cased: google-genai matches 'global' / 'us' / 'eu' case-sensitively."""
    return (os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_LOCATION).strip().lower()

The google-genai client SDK requires exact case matching when specifying regional and multi-regional endpoints. This helper reads GEMINI_LOCATION, applies fallback to DEFAULT_GEMINI_LOCATION ("global"), strips surrounding whitespace, and ensures lowercase formatting to avoid SDK routing errors.

docs.title: openrouter_base_url()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def openrouter_base_url() -> str:

Description: Resolves and cleanses the base URL for OpenRouter or OpenAI-compatible gateway endpoints, removing trailing slashes and redundant /v1 path segments.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: Clean base URL without a trailing slash or /v1 suffix.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def openrouter_base_url() -> str:
    """OPENROUTER_BASE_URL without a trailing '/' or '/v1' (OpenAI SDK style); paths add '/v1/...'."""
    base = (os.getenv("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL).strip().rstrip("/")
    return base.removesuffix("/v1")

The OpenAI client specification and REST dispatchers expect clean root URLs onto which paths like /v1/chat/completions or /v1/models can be appended. This helper strips whitespace, removes trailing slashes via rstrip("/"), and trims trailing /v1 segments via removesuffix("/v1").
